hypotheses.name: Nobody's hurrying on Hormuz — 60% → 65% (RAISED)
hypotheses.d: Its first fact that BEATS a rival instead of merely fitting itself. On 30 Aug the US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak after observing Guard personnel preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait — two days after CENTCOM declared the lanes fully cleared, and while Muscat negotiates a minesweeping calendar. The 08-30 audit had installed a genuine rival — a physical clock, minesweeping simply takes time — and ruled this hypothesis must beat it. A physical clock runs down; this one is being rewound, by the exact actor the hypothesis named in advance. Capped at +5 on three counts kept in front: CENTCOM is the interested party and 'observed preparations' is unpublished intelligence used to justify a strike; Al Jazeera published a technical challenge on 31 Aug to whether Iran can even mine by rocket as claimed; and IRGC counter-coercion against a blockade that has redirected 83 vessels, disabled three and boarded two explains the same act without any rent motive. Not pre-event.

Kinetic down, jurisdiction up. NOT moved — this is the same signal that bought +5 on 08-26, and re-marking on the continuation of its own evidence is the double-count the audit named. The important item is against my own test: if Beijing has DECLARED the patrols permanent, their persistence through the Sept 24 visit is close to uninformative. Re-specified now, in advance and stricter — the informative observation on 09-23→09-25 is a boarding, an inspection, or a first-time-area incursion. Mere presence no longer counts as confirmation.

hypotheses.name: Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it holds at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Falsifiers: token export volumes, Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing not actually swinging off the Middle East, or the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appearing. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Note it is DISTINCT from 'The Portfolio State' below, which is about the vehicle rather than the motive.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — HELD 52%
hypotheses.d: Confirming but shared, therefore ambience: Treasury again held back on Chinese financial institutions, with mainstream reporting now naming the mechanism outright — designating them 'could create tensions before Xi's visit'. Bessent's promised weekly cadence hit banks but no Chinese one, and at the G20 he pushed severing Iran financial ties while China dissented. Both the leverage read and the ordinary 'Washington won't detonate its own summit' read predict all of it. The strongest weekly argument AGAINST, logged rather than absorbed: the US struck Iran on three consecutive nights and took Iranian fire onto three Arab host states. Deliberate slow-walking for leverage sits badly with sustained kinetic escalation that raises the cost of the thing being slow-walked — that counterweight is what holds the number at 52.

hypotheses.name: A pre-announcement leak into oil futures — 40% → 34% (biggest mover)
hypotheses.d: Its lead conditional has now gone unfired across three weeks containing the most violently market-moving Iran news since April — the 30 Aug Larak strike, three nights of exchanges, two struck VLCCs, Brent to ~$95 — with not one reported nine-figure pre-announcement episode. The file is confirmed as historical and bounded: DOJ is probing four trades totalling ~$2.6bn, all inside a five-week window that closed in April — Mar 23 (>$500m, ~15 min before Trump's delay post), Apr 7 ($960m before the ceasefire), Apr 17 ($760m, ~20 min before Iran said Hormuz was open), Apr 21 ($430m before the extension). CORRECTION BANKED AGAINST THIS ENTRY: the ledger's earlier '~$2.2bn cluster' for Mar 23 and its '~$7bn' aggregate are both withdrawn as over-wide constructions. The cut is made on the hypothesis's own written terms, not on a preferred reading — a conditional set at 60% has burned three of fourteen weeks in the best environment it will ever get and produced nothing. The cut is only −6 because of one genuinely new structural fact: investigators are running a SEPARATE probe into prediction-market activity on the same developments, and the same foreknowledge reaching two unrelated venues is hard to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. Split now: deliberate leak 34 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 36 / coincidence 10. Still the only entry whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event.

hypotheses.name: NEW · The Portfolio State — coercion converted into sovereign equity, statute retrofitted
hypotheses.d: Strongest form: the US is converting military and sanctions leverage into permanent state equity in strategic supply chains, with the legal authority written to fit transactions rather than the reverse — Venezuela being the first hydrocarbon use of a template already run in chips and critical minerals. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing licensing a design read at all: Senate NDAA FY2027 §1051 was marked up in MID-JUNE — ten weeks before the 29 Aug deal — creating a DoD Equity Investment Account, authorising OSC equity to $500m and capping any single position at 40% of the entity; the Venezuela stake is 35%, inside a cap that does not legally exist yet. Add DoD's own $400m/15% stake in MP Materials with 100% offtake (structurally identical to Venezuela's '20% of output at cost'), House Oversight already demanding an accounting of Venezuelan oil revenue on 23 Feb, and CFR's tally of 26 government equity deals worth ~$23.9bn. It opens at only 25% because the boring, incompetence and patronage readings are all strong: think tanks have been publicly naming and counting this pattern since 2025 (a policy, not a plot); the Pentagon's own spokesman flatly DENIES that OSC takes equity while WSJ reports it doing so, which is improvisation not design; and a 100-year concession over 65bn bbl routed to one politically connected operator with no published contract is better explained as spoils allocation. Above all the base rate is enormous — Anglo-Persian 1914, the RFC, GM/Chrysler 2009 — so the design premium must be small. NOT a conspiracy claim and must never be scored as one: it requires no secrecy at all, only anticipation, and the honest gap is that I cannot name the operator who executes the warrants. Key test: does the ENACTED NDAA widen §1051 beyond critical minerals to energy, or raise the cap, by 31 Dec (45%)? Scope enacted unchanged kills the design read.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 25% → 22% (CUT, sixth session running)
hypotheses.d: The week finally produced Russia-Iran material and it is the wrong KIND. Moscow said publicly on 01 Sep that air defence is the main focus of military-technical cooperation with Iran, alongside a reported 500 Verba MANPADS and 2,500 missiles and continued fighter deliveries. That is the resupply leg — already priced at 7/10 under 'means'. It moves nothing: it is announced by TASS, an interested party publishing its own helpfulness and the structural opposite of a covert channel; the opportunism branch predicts arms sales to a client at war identically, so under the standing rule it is ambience; and after six sessions there is still ZERO documentary evidence Moscow has influenced Tehran's negotiating position, which is the actual claim. Arms transfers are not persuasion. Cut rather than held because a decay rule that bites only on its deadline is a cliff, not decay. Clock unchanged: 15% on 30 Sep absent documentary evidence, retire below 10%.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Nothing resolved this week, and one file addition cuts against it: the summit's Iran content is now openly reported as an explicit US ask — Chinese pressure on Tehran to reopen the strait — with Beijing expected to want Taiwan concessions in return. An openly negotiated Iran-for-Taiwan trade is this hypothesis's RIVAL, not its confirmation; the secret-package version needs the deal hidden, and the deal is being conducted in headlines. Retirement trigger unchanged; the test runs on schedule on 24 Sept.

brief.head: Dutch central bank pulls 86 tonnes of gold out of North America
brief.h: De Nederlandsche Bank shifted 86 tonnes from New York and Ottawa to London between March and August, cutting its US-vaulted share from 31.3 per cent to 18.5, and named geopolitical unrest as the reason.
brief.t: A central bank does not move metal for the exercise. DNB holds 612.4 tonnes worth about 72 billion euros, and the distribution just changed shape: New York and Ottawa down to 18.5 per cent each, London up from 18.1 to 32.1, the Netherlands untouched at 30.8. Only about 27 tonnes physically travelled - the rest was done by selling roughly 59 tonnes in New York and buying the same quantity in London, which tells you the object being moved is not bullion but jurisdiction. The stated reason is deployability: DNB president Olaf Sleijpen said gold in London can be traded more easily than gold in New York or Ottawa, and gold you cannot swap or lend inside a day is not a reserve, it is a museum exhibit.
brief.context: The rail is older than the headline. Germany repatriated hundreds of tonnes from New York and Paris after 2013, and the Banque de France finished pulling its last bars out of the New York Fed earlier this year, so a euro-area central bank reducing US-vaulted gold is now a pattern with at least three members rather than a first. The deciding desk is DNB's own reserve-management committee, not the Dutch finance ministry - which is exactly why the language is technical. What makes it worth a card is the timing rather than the act: it lands while the US Treasury is buying back the long end and while a NATO ally is being asked to reimburse Washington for Ukraine aid. The base rate on custody shifts is that they are slow, quiet and rarely reversed. The honest caution is that London is not neutral ground either - it is where the loan and swap market lives, which is a commercial argument, not a sovereignty one.

angles.effect: Gains real optionality - reserves it can mobilise inside a crisis day rather than a week - and gets to say so in the dullest possible language
Loses custody share and, more importantly, the default-vault status that made the question never worth asking
Gains the deepest slice of a European official holding, and the lending and fee business that follows the metal
Pays if the marketability story is later read as the polite version - a confidence cost that only arrives if a second and third bank follow

dec.kill: The New York Fed's earmarked-gold series showing no sustained decline in total foreign holdings over the next two quarters, and no other euro-area central bank announcing a similar shift. That would make this housekeeping, not a trend.

consp.claim: That the Dutch move is insider knowledge made physical - that DNB pulled the metal because it expects the United States to seize, lend out or fail to deliver foreign-held gold, and that the official marketability explanation is cover for a vault run that ordinary savers are not invited to.
consp.spread: A /pol/ thread headed DUTCH PULL ALL THEIR GOLD OUT OF AMERICA opened this evening, running alongside the standing Precious Metals General on /biz/ at over 300 replies and a counter-thread arguing gold buyers are being set up.
consp.read: The custodial-default frame, and its kernel is unusually solid for this board: the movement is real, officially announced, and DNB itself cited geopolitical unrest. Where it breaks is the inference - the same bank left 30.8 per cent in the Netherlands and moved the metal to London rather than home, which is a liquidity decision, not a flight to sovereignty. This is downstream of the 2013 Bundesbank episode, which is the template every one of these threads is quietly reusing.

brief.head: Bessent blames Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries for price shock
brief.h: Asked why the cost of living is high, the Treasury Secretary named Kyiv's attacks on Russian energy assets before he named the Iran war - on the same day Trump said Washington will bill European governments for aid already sent to Ukraine.
brief.t: Read the ordering, because the ordering is the policy. Bessent said the world is going through an energy shock due to both the war in Ukraine, because Ukraine has decided that they want to blow up Russian energy assets and refined products, and then the conflict in Iran. That sentence quietly reclassifies Russian refining capacity from a legitimate target of economic warfare into a global public good whose destruction raises your fuel bill. Follow the incentive rather than the sentiment: an administration that owns the pump price going into the midterms needs an explanation that is not the strait its own campaign has kept shut for six months. Ukraine is the only candidate that costs nothing domestically to blame.
brief.context: The rail here is standard sanctions doctrine, which for three years has held that you end an aggressor's war by degrading the export earnings that fund it - and refined product is the highest-value part of that. The deciding desk is Treasury, specifically the office that writes the energy carve-outs, and it is the same desk that built the Economic D-Day programme against Iran, so this is not a man who thinks energy infrastructure is off limits in principle. The coalition filter explains the rest: the audience that prices this quarter cares about diesel, the implementing class prices the decade, and when they collide the podium speaks to the first. Base rate: blame-shifting language from a finance ministry has historically preceded a negotiating position rather than a sanctions change, which is why the kill criterion below is about instruments and not adjectives. Former Ukrainian official Anton Gerashchenko's public reply - that the Iran war has moved the energy market significantly more - is the mainstream counter, and on the physical board it is the better-supported one.

angles.effect: Gains a non-Hormuz explanation for a pump price it politically owns, delivered by the most credible market voice in the cabinet
Pays - pressure to wind down the one campaign that measurably reduces Russian war revenue, framed as a favour to the world economy
Gains without asking - its refining capacity recategorised as infrastructure the world needs kept intact
Pay twice: the gas price, and now a demand to reimburse Washington for aid already delivered

dec.kill: A published Treasury or EIA decomposition attributing the current price to Ukrainian strikes rather than to the Hormuz closure, or new US sanctions on a Russian refinery within a month. Either would show the framing is analysis rather than positioning.

consp.claim: That the reimbursement demand and the blame are one move rather than two - that Washington is retroactively converting alliance aid into a debt owed by Europe, and that shielding Russian refining is a pre-agreed term of a settlement being negotiated over Kyiv's head.
consp.spread: A /pol/ thread headed Trump demands refund from Europe for Ukraine aid, linking the Reuters wire and reading it approvingly as tribute, alongside the two permanent Ukraine generals running at 265 and 168 replies.
consp.read: The tribute frame, and the checkable half is on the record: the President did say hundreds of billions were given free of charge and that Washington will be asking for that money, and the Treasury Secretary did put Ukrainian strikes ahead of Iran. What is asserted is the coordination - that these are terms of a deal rather than two politicians reaching for the same nearby argument. Note the frame is being cheered rather than feared, which is itself the finding: this audience reads a demand on allies as strength, and that domestic incentive is exactly what makes the move likely to be repeated.

brief.head: Carmakers press Congress to ban Chinese vehicles before it adjourns
brief.h: The Alliance for Automotive Innovation, speaking for GM, Ford, Toyota, Volkswagen, Hyundai, Honda and Stellantis, asked for a permanent vehicle, software and hardware ban written into law before the session ends on 3 January - hours after Volkswagen's board approved a plan flagging up to 50,000 job cuts.
brief.t: The security argument is doing work a tariff cannot. A tariff is an executive instrument, which means a president can trade it away across a table in an afternoon; a statute has to be repealed. With Xi's state visit twenty-one days out and a tariff truce both capitals want to keep, the industry is trying to take the concession off the board before anyone can offer it. Alliance chief John Bozzella's wording is the tell - Chinese automakers are dumping subsidised vehicles with connected software and hardware around the world - because it fuses a trade complaint with a data-security complaint, and only the second reliably passes a legislature. The Volkswagen number on the same day is the honest subtext: this is a cost problem being answered with a legal wall.
brief.context: The rail predates the headline. A connected-vehicle rule already restricts Chinese hardware and software in cars sold in the US, so what is being sought is permanence and scope, not a new idea. The deciding desks are Commerce and the congressional trade committees rather than the White House, which is precisely why the industry went to Congress and not to the podium. Base rate on lame-duck industrial legislation with an election in view: low, and lower still when it cuts across an active summit track the President has invested in. Watch the split it creates inside the coalition - Detroit and the US plants of foreign makers want the wall, while dealers, retailers and anyone selling into a price-sensitive market do not, and that fault line is where the bill will either die or get narrowed.

angles.effect: Gain a permanent floor under their home market that no future summit can trade away
Pay in price - the cheapest vehicles in the world stay out, and the cost arrives as a sticker rather than a tariff line
Gains a concrete grievance to carry into the 24 September visit, and evidence for its case that the truce is not being kept
Loses a bargaining chip if the ban becomes statute - which is the entire reason the ask is for statute

dec.kill: No committee markup before the session ends, or the administration opposing the bill to protect the summit. Either would show the tariff is still the live instrument and the letter was a lobbying position.

consp.claim: That European carmaking is not being restructured but converted - that Volkswagen closing plants and cutting tens of thousands of jobs is the visible half of a rearmament programme, with the same lines redirected to military production and Germany quietly militarising under cover of an industrial crisis.
consp.spread: A /pol/ thread headed NUCLEAR HAPPENING claiming VW closes their car factories and starts producing military equipment, opened as the job-cut wire landed.
consp.read: The conversion frame, and it is not absurd. Kernel: German defence procurement has expanded sharply since 2022, at least one automotive plant has already been taken over by a defence manufacturer, and dual-use conversion of vehicle lines is real and documented. What the thread adds is intent and scale, presenting a cost-driven restructuring the company has been running for two years as a disguised state programme. The boring reading is in Volkswagen's own words - a competitiveness gap against Chinese manufacturers, which is the same force that produced today's letter to Congress.

brief.head: Senegal wins a $2.2bn IMF deal and opens its debt to restructuring
brief.h: A three-year staff-level agreement reached on 1 September follows the discovery of more than $11bn of previously misreported borrowing - about a quarter of a $40bn economy - with public debt near 132 per cent of GDP and every international bond trading below 50 cents.
brief.t: The number to hold is not the loan, it is the carve-out. Dakar's finance ministry says it has agreed an enhanced common framework to restore debt sustainability, and that everything issued in CFA francs sits outside the restructuring perimeter. That one sentence decides who is senior before a negotiation has started: domestic banks and franc-zone creditors are protected, external bondholders take the write-down. Follow the money and the reason is structural rather than moral - the CFA franc is pegged to the euro and backed by a monetary union, so haircutting it would transmit a Senegalese problem into a fifteen-country currency arrangement. Hidden debt is a governance failure; who eats it is a monetary decision.
brief.context: The rail is the G20 Common Framework, built after 2020 to get Chinese and private creditors into the same room, and used so far by Zambia, Chad, Ethiopia and Ghana with a time from request to deal measured in years rather than months. The template underneath is Mozambique's tuna bonds - undisclosed borrowing found after the fact, an IMF programme frozen, a restructuring that eventually landed and a decade of litigation. The deciding desks are the IMF Executive Board and the BCEAO, the West African central bank that owns the peg. Base rate worth stating plainly: staff-level agreements convert to board approval in the large majority of cases, but the tranches then arrive against reviews, so the money is a schedule, not a cheque. What would change the read is the perimeter moving.

angles.effect: Gains a financing anchor and a story in which the hidden debt was inherited and disclosed rather than concealed
Pay - already marked below 50 cents, and now formally inside a restructuring perimeter the CFA debt sits outside of

angles.party: Domestic banks and the franc zone
angles.effect: Shielded by the carve-out, which protects the peg and the regional banking system at the bondholders' expense
Gains a Common Framework test case in a country it can plausibly stabilise, after a run of slow and contested ones

dec.kill: Executive Board approval slipping past year end, or CFA-denominated debt being pulled into the restructuring perimeter. The second would mean the seniority carve-out did not hold, and the whole read changes.

brief.head: Iran strikes US bases in Kuwait and the UAE as the war widens
brief.h: Tehran's army says missiles and drones hit satellite communications, warehouses and fighter hangars at Ahmed al-Jaber in Kuwait and troop areas and radars at Al Minhad in the Emirates; Kuwait confirmed it was engaging an attack, while the UAE said it handled a drone over its territorial waters and denied the base was struck.
brief.t: This is horizontal escalation, and the distinction matters more than the damage. Iran cannot reach the United States, so it raises the price of hosting it - the target is not the hangar, it is the calculation inside a Gulf ruler's cabinet about what the American presence now costs in airspace, insurance and tourism. Notice the asymmetry in the claims: Iran describes damage, the hosts confirm only the attempt, and no US confirmation of a hit has appeared. Both sides are managing the same fact in opposite directions, because an intercepted missile lets everyone keep the equilibrium and a landed one does not.
brief.context: The rail is the interception-dependent equilibrium that has held this entire war: every volley intercepted, no American killed, no US-flagged hull struck - which is exactly the published condition this desk requires before moving its risk state to the top. The Emirates becoming a struck host widens the set of surfaces on which that equilibrium can fail. The deciding desk is not CENTCOM but the host cabinets, since a Gulf state restricting offensive sorties from its soil would constrain the air campaign faster than anything Tehran can do kinetically. Base rate: host states have historically absorbed this kind of fire and quietly raised their price rather than expelling the force, because expulsion forfeits the security guarantee that justified the basing in the first place. What would change it is a host-state civilian casualty, which converts an American problem into a domestic one.

angles.effect: Gains a demonstration of reach at low cost - the claim of damage travels whether or not the damage happened
Pay in airspace, insurance and the political cost of hosting a campaign whose tempo they do not set
Gains proof its air defences hold, and pays in the slow erosion of host tolerance that no interception rate fixes
Pay immediately - premia reprice on the attempt, not on the outcome

dec.kill: A Gulf host publicly restricting US offensive operations from its territory, or a confirmed American death or struck US-flagged hull. Any of those breaks the equilibrium this read depends on.

consp.claim: That the war's official duration and scope are a running fraud, with the thread header keeping its own tally at Day 187 of what it calls the four-day special military operation to regime change Iran and Day 1061 of the two-day limited offensive to end Hezbollah, and reading the reported private discussion of declaring the war over while deployments extend into 2027 as the confession.
consp.spread: Persia Israel General on /pol/ carrying the day-count in its subject line at 167 replies, alongside a separate thread on the reported White House discussion of declaring the Iran war over.
consp.read: The duration-fraud frame, and its kernel is the strongest thing on the board: the sold duration and the actual duration are separated by a factor of dozens, and the deployment order genuinely does now reach into 2027 while the possibility of declaring the war over is being reported. That gap is a real coalition tell - a war sold as days and run in years is evidence about who holds the file, which is a standing part of this desk's method rather than a fringe reading. What the frame adds is deliberate deception, where planning failure fits the record at least as well.

lesson: Today's lesson is a mechanism with a name, and once you have it you will see it in half a dozen borders. The political scientist Kelly Greenhill called it coercive engineered migration - the use, or the threatened use, of population movements as an instrument of statecraft. It works on a specific kind of target: a state with liberal asylum obligations, a free press and a domestic opposition, because those three things convert a crowd at a fence into a governing crisis within about forty-eight hours. And its elegance is that the coercer need not act at all. A neighbouring state can generate the entire effect by omission - by standing its border patrols down for one afternoon - which leaves no treaty violated, nothing attributable, and no proportionate response available, since you cannot bomb a country for failing to police a beach. Greenhill assembled roughly fifty-six cases since 1951 and found that most attempts extracted at least partial concessions, which is a striking number and one worth handling carefully: it is a single-author dataset, and quiet failures are exactly the cases hardest to observe, so treat it as a strong indication rather than a settled rate. The clearest worked example is the one directly behind today's Ceuta story. In May 2021 Morocco let several thousand people swim around the same breakwater after Spain hosted a Polisario leader for medical treatment; within a year Madrid had reversed six decades of policy and endorsed Moroccan autonomy over Western Sahara. That is what the instrument buys. So here is what it predicts now, in a form you can score: if the July crossing was coercion rather than an accident of a court ruling and a viral post, the payment will not be visible at the border - it will appear over the next twelve months as a Spanish concession on Western Sahara, on fisheries access, or on customs at Ceuta and Melilla. If a year passes with no such concession, the coercion read was wrong and the boring explanation was right. That is the honest test, and it is the reason to learn the mechanism rather than to pick a side in the row about it.

events.label: Strait of Hormuz
events.note: Fourth consecutive night of US strikes on air defences, radars, maritime assets and mine-laying capability around the strait. Transits fell to as few as six vessels in a day against a ten-day average near thirteen and a pre-war norm around eighty-five

events.label: Kuhestak, Hormozgan
events.note: A US strike hit a house holding a wedding here on 1-2 September along with a nearby telecommunications tower, killing four named civilians including a four-year-old and wounding more than sixty. CENTCOM contested the sourcing of the report, not the strike

events.label: Ahmed al-Jaber AB, Kuwait
events.note: Iran's army claims missiles and suicide drones against satellite communications, equipment warehouses and fighter hangars here. Kuwait's army confirmed it was engaging the attack; no host-state confirmation of damage, which is the honest limit of what is known

events.label: Al Minhad AB, UAE
events.note: Iran claims strikes on US positions and radar systems here - the Emirates becoming the sixth host state to take fire in this war, and the newest surface on which an interception-dependent equilibrium can fail

events.label: Kharg Island
events.note: Still undamaged and still the subject of the 30 September falsifier clock. Handles about 90 per cent of Iranian crude exports; the March raid hit military sites here and deliberately spared the loading terminals

events.label: Ceuta
events.note: Sanchez told parliament there were no advance alerts before the 30-31 July crossing of some sixty to seventy thousand people, while a National Police report to a judge alleges Moroccan security personnel helped direct it and two dated police warnings are reported to have gone to the interior ministry

events.label: Leipzig/Halle Airport
events.note: Britain summoned Russia's charge d'affaires today over the 4 August explosive drone at the airport used to move munitions to Ukraine, widening the attribution Germany made last week. Berlin closes the Bonn consulate on 18 September; Moscow promises to mirror

events.label: Rotterdam / TTF hub
events.note: Dutch front-month gas near a three-year high with EU storage around 62 per cent, some 17 points below the seasonal norm and the thinnest for the date since records began in 2011. Roughly a fifth of world LNG normally transits Hormuz

events.label: Vladivostok
events.note: Putin told the Eastern Economic Forum there is a chance of an agreement and confirmed contacts with Kyiv continue on an ongoing basis, primarily through intelligence channels - six days after his spokesman called negotiations a deep pause with no proposals whatsoever

events.label: Odesa
events.note: Russia continues striking port export facilities and the energy grid before the heating season while the diplomatic track is described as promising. Tempo has not changed since the language did

events.label: Tokyo
events.note: Yen to a one-month high of 156.15 on rate-rise bets before the 18 September BoJ decision; ten-year JGB near 3 per cent, the highest since 1996. The world's cheap funding leg is repricing and the transmission runs through every asset bought with borrowed yen

events.label: Beijing
events.note: Twenty-one days to the Xi state visit, with Washington preparing a 7.5 per cent overcapacity tariff layer sized to land exactly on the 20 per cent ceiling Beijing says it was promised. China pulled out of the Gwangju Biennale over a Taiwan exhibition - symbolic friction, not a quarantine signal

fired: NO NEW FIRE today, and the 1 September Hormuz fire is NOT re-counted. That wire fired on the stricter 27 August wording - an attack on a US-flagged or US-escorted vessel, or an attack Iran publicly claims - and dating a fire exactly once is the whole point of having narrowed it. A fourth night of exchanges is continuation of a fired wire, not a new one

NOT fired, and it remains the limit of everything above: no struck US-flagged hull, no confirmed American death. Iran put its fire into Kuwaiti and Emirati air bases and Kuwait's army confirmed it was engaging missiles and drones launched from Iran. The intercepted-volley equilibrium has now held for a fourth night, and it is arithmetic rather than restraint

NOT fired, checked and logged so each non-fire is scoreable: no blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank; no strike on Kharg's loading terminals; no awarded dredging or terminal contract in Venezuela; no concrete poured past the prohibited level at Kishanganga; no Kremlin acceptance of any limited ceasefire; no Taiwan mobilization indicator; no EU emergency intervention in the gas market

WIRE HYGIENE - the board has now taken fire on six host states and had no wire covering the hosts' own politics, which is the surface where this escalation actually converts into a political event. Corrected below. A second gap, on the yen funding leg, is corrected at the same time and paid for with a new forecast rather than only with a wire

Data gap: GDELT was unreachable (URLError) on both tested keywords - Strait of Hormuz and gold reserves - for the THIRD consecutive session. Recorded as a gap, not as zero. Three dark sessions running makes this a failed instrument rather than an outage, and the honest consequence is that the news-volume channel has contributed nothing to any update this week
armed: NEW - Gulf host defection: a GCC government publicly restricting US offensive use of its territory or airspace, or formally conditioning basing on de-escalation talks with Tehran, before 15 December. That is the observable that converts a venue into a party, and it is the sequel nobody is pricing

NEW - BoJ 18 September: a policy-rate rise accompanied by USD/JPY through 150. That is the confirmation leg on the newly opened GEO-025, and the point at which a Tokyo rate decision becomes a global margin call
A struck US-flagged hull or a confirmed American death - the falsifier on the whole intercepted-volley equilibrium, and still the only escalation trigger left unfired in the strait

An Iranian strike that kills nationals of a Gulf host state rather than only targeting US facilities on their soil. That is what would convert Kuwait, the Emirates, Bahrain and Jordan from venues into parties

A war-risk re-rating of the southern Hormuz corridor by the Joint War Committee, or a withdrawal of the US clearance claim - the actuarial event that governs GEO-001 far more than any diplomatic announcement
A strike on Kharg's LOADING terminals as opposed to its military sites - it would convert the 30 August video from theatre into a warning order and re-rate GEO-001, GEO-003 and GEO-009 together
Europe/energy: an EU emergency intervention in the gas market before 15 November - a price cap, mandatory demand curtailment, or a storage-target waiver

Publication of the US overcapacity finding with the 7.5 per cent layer actually imposed before 24 September - versus a quiet delay past the summit. That single observable separates a coalition standard being built from a chip being waved

An awarded, funded dredging contract or dedicated heavy-crude terminal tender in the Orinoco or Lake Maracaibo channel - what GEO-022 resolves on, and the line between opportunistic spoils and a pre-built heavy-barrel rail
Publication of the two Spanish police intelligence notes dated 28 and 29 July with their distribution lists - the document that settles the Ceuta warnings question in either direction
A failed or heavily tailed JGB or gilt auction - the point at which the long-end repricing stops being a price move and becomes a funding event
Scholar-owned: IRGC/Basij defection (Takeyh) - casualty-recruitment crossover (Kofman) - PLA purge tempo (Fravel)

watch: Whether a second euro-area central bank announces a reduction of its US-vaulted gold within ninety days. One is housekeeping and DNB has given a technical reason; two makes it a rail, and moves the reserve-custody question from marketability to counterparty risk

Whether Kuwait or the UAE publicly restricts US offensive sorties from their soil after taking fire. Host tolerance, not Iranian capability, is the binding constraint on the air campaign - and the escalation step this desk published still requires a confirmed American death or a struck US-flagged hull

Whether the Chinese vehicle, software and hardware ban gets a committee markup before the 3 January adjournment, and whether the White House backs it with the Xi state visit on 24 September. A statute the President did not want is a very different signal from a letter he ignored

Whether the IMF Executive Board approves Senegal's programme and whether CFA-denominated debt stays outside the restructuring perimeter. The perimeter, not the headline number, decides who actually pays

Whether the Panama Canal Authority's 15 September cut to 32 transits a day takes effect, now joined by a UK minister telling households to hold several days of supplies after a supersize El Nino warning. The same physical story at two ends - the chokepoint and the shelf
